column2: The Neighbouring Estates Declare Independence

The neighbouring Baltic government has renounced imperial allegiance and asks our diet to join its common defence. Acceptance commits this province to the same struggle against Russia, while leaving the future constitution for a congress after peace. The diet can instead preserve its imperial charter.
Join the common struggle and defend provincial independence.
Preserve our charter beneath the Russian crown.
Delegates for the Baltic Constitutional Conference

Peace permits the Baltic governments to consider a common constitution. The convening diet will put a ducal union, a Livonian crown or a federal republic before the delegates. Sending delegates gives this province a place in that debate, accession still requires a separate ratification of the proposed settlement.
Send delegates and reserve the diet's right of ratification.
Retain separate government and decline the conference.

The Baltic War of Independence

Provincial proclamations have become a common struggle against the Russian crown. The participating diets retain their own administrations while their commanders coordinate the defence of the ports and inland roads. Victory can secure provincial independence, it cannot by itself settle the authority of a future Baltic government.
Defend the proclamations and coordinate the common defence.
Draft a federal union of the Baltic duchies.
Draft a united Kingdom of Livonia.
Draft a federal Baltic republic.
Keep separate provincial states and a common defensive understanding.
The Baltic Constitutional Conference

Delegates meet after the struggle to put their independence into constitutional form. A federal ducal union would preserve the provincial estates beneath a common crown. A Livonian kingdom would unite them under a royal government, while a federal republic would rest upon elected institutions. Separate sovereign governments remain possible. Every accession requires the provincial diet's assent and the recovery of its capital.
Separate Governments After the Peace

The diets retain their separate sovereign governments. Cooperation in defence and trade can continue without transferring their administrations to a common crown or assembly. A later congress may revisit union, but the present settlement preserves each province's right to decide its own constitution.
Preserve provincial independence and continue cooperation.
The Provincial Capital Under Occupation

Imperial troops have taken the provincial capital. Deputies and officers continue their work from the districts still held by the independent government, while refugees carry news of the occupation along the roads. The proclamation survives only if the province can regain a secure seat of government before the peace.
Preserve the provincial administration and seek to recover the capital.
The Diet Returns to Its Provincial Capital

The independent government has recovered its provincial capital. Offices reopen and the diet resumes its sittings, but the military struggle has not yet ended. The recovered city gives the proclamation a secure seat and renews hopes that peace may leave the province free to frame its own future.
Restore the offices and continue the common defence.
The Unfinished Baltic Settlement

Independence left the constitutional settlement unfinished. The diet confirms the provincial institutions chosen before the war and recalls the neighbouring delegates to consider a common government. Existing provincial sovereignty remains in force until the diets ratify a concrete proposal.
Confirm the provincial government and recall the constitutional conference.

The United Estates Settle the Peace

The provinces entered the struggle under a common government. Their surviving estates now settle the constitution for peace. They may confirm the federal ducal union, place the country beneath a Livonian crown or establish a federal republic. Retaining the existing settlement is also possible. These choices preserve the territory and sovereignty won during the war.
The Diet Withdraws Its Present Proposal

The conditions under which the estates called this sitting have changed. The government withdraws the present proposal and resumes ordinary business. A declaration or congress can be considered again when the provincial capital and diplomatic position permit it.
Resume the business of the provincial administration.
